title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: additive Cheon v27 (prime class lists, birthday law tested against its own null at two scales, exact level closed by off-diagonal injectivity, proven 2.63x availability)

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.416 (at least 0.39 required; the birthday-model value 1 - e^-0.55 = 0.42305 for the coverage set |U*B*G^-1|, charged a 1.5% multiplicative law slowdown: >= 0.985 x 0.42305 = 0.4167, floor-stated 0.416. The law is tested as a law - against random sets at the same parameters, its own null - at two scales 64x apart in d, under the exact declared block rule (ka = 2*n*d*LN//X2 + 1 with LN = floor(ln X2) + 1, no fallback; ascending blocks; X1*X2 < r asserted): at d = 2^8 (r ~ 2^29.84, n = 588, ka = 184) the construction matches the law to the fourth decimal (0.4238 against 0.4238, closer than the random null's 0.4231), and at d = 2^4 (n = 338, ka = 74) the construction and the random null deviate identically (0.4219 both, +0.61%); the matched integer-list control at d = 2^4 - the same r, m, n, X1, X2, ka and prime blocks with all-integer class lists - measures 0.3296, a 22.4% deviation (the composite multiplicative family the construction eliminates), and the smallest-integers-in-H baseline measures 0.3952 (-6.9%: structured sets deviate, the prime construction does not). The exact level is closed by off-diagonal ratio injectivity: every element is a product a*b of two primes from disjoint ranges (a in (2^81, 2^82], b a prime <= 2^70, baby/giant blocks disjoint), b/c = b'/c' (mod r) with b != c forces (b, c) = (b', c') because bc' = b'c as integers (|bc' - b'c| < X2^2 = 2^140 < r), and likewise for the a-ratios (|aa''' - a''a'| < X1^2 = 2^164 < r); the unit ratio's diagonal preimages are exactly the counted shared-class-prefix family - a same-class prime pair with shared consumed prefix t loses 6*(t-1) distinct values - counted exactly per run (3,858 at d = 2^4; 972 at d = 2^8) and bounded at production at 6*(N_A/2)^2*(L2-1)/d = 2^172.6 values = 2^-61 of the 6N_BN_G pair slots, a bound under H2, not an extrapolation in d (the u != u' exceptional family adds at most 2^151 values, covered); every other coincidence is a genuinely modular product event, which is what the birthday law prices. The end-to-end toy attack confirms the law: 0.55 over 40 shuffled trials and 0.4375 over 16 fixed-order trials against 0.4267 predicted, every recovered scalar correct) over the uniform challenge. The algorithm is Cheon's p-1 baby-step/giant-step in the subgroup H of 2^20-th powers. Its baby and giant sets are products a*b of two primes in H (a a prime in (2^81, 2^82], b a prime <= 2^70 with chi(a)+chi(b)=0), walked in increasing order at one batched affine G1 addition per element. It uses the 6-element symmetry group {+-1, +-lambda, +-lambda^2} via the hash key min(y, p-y). Provenance: the declared dependency cbadde77; every identity, itemisation and bound below is this package's own, restated in proof.md and re-verified by this package's runs. The per-element budgets: canonical y 30 (itemised ~25), walk bookkeeping 100 (itemised ~75), hash insert/lookup 240 (a complete per-transfer accounting: endpoint 61 plus six radix-1024 relay stages of 29 instructions each - 18 word moves, 4 destination selection, 4 queue updates, 3 control - over the sharded table; the linear-probing and sharding model is evidenced by a 16,384-key toy check measuring 1.486/2.512 mean probes against the 1.5/2.5 bounds and shard loads within 2.55 sigma). Its total work W(n) = W(2^20) is at most 2^116.958777 target-group-operation equivalents. This includes the distributed hash-table inserts and lookups, walk bookkeeping, per-prime tables, character precomputation and sieves, collision verification, the d-th root, the final mu_d search and input checks. Preprocessing (challenge-independent work) is at most 2^115.968 and is included. Peak memory is at most 2^122.9 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice. Heuristics: H1 (the birthday law with the charged 1.5% slowdown, tested against its own null at two scales 64x apart in d; exact level closed by off-diagonal injectivity and bounded at 2^-61 of pair slots at production); H2 (the primes <= 2^70 and the primes in (2^81, 2^82] equidistribute over the chi-classes, affecting only how many primes are needed; the interval supply is a proven Rosser-Schoenfeld lower bound at 2^74.716, a 2.63x slack over N_A ~ 2^73.32); and expected-cost hashing and sharding, evidenced by a 16,384-key probe/shard toy check. All are disclosed and supported by toy experiments at their stated scope. This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.

experiments.purpose: One run with five parts. (1) Recomputes the cost ledger at K = 0.55 (canonical y 30, hash 240, bookkeeping 100; every charge asserted above its itemised count), the exact score, the preprocessing output, the PROVEN prime-availability interval lower bound (Rosser-Schoenfeld) and the shared-class-prefix lost-value bound. (2) The law's null test at two scales (ascending prime blocks by the declared rule ka = 2*n*d*LN//X2 + 1 with no fallback, X1*X2 < r asserted in code, exact bitmap counts of U*B*G^-1 converted in 1 MB chunks): d = 2^4 with the random-set null, the smallest-integers-in-H baseline and the matched integer-list control at the same r, m, n, X1, X2, ka and prime blocks; d = 2^8 (cov_bits-driven) with the random-set null. Every point reports the exact shared-class-prefix lost-value count. (3) A 16,384-key hash_probe check on keys from the structured production-style walk. (4) The full end-to-end toy attack (shuffled, 40 trials) on a 24-bit j = 0 curve with d = 2^6. (5) A fixed-order attack run (16 trials) under the deterministic set rule. Toy results are evidence at their scale only. Input: K, cov_bits, cov_logd, atk_bits, atk_logd, trials, gmax, seed.
